summary: Agent implemented the checkbox directly in index.html on the first turn (~31s, 3 tool calls: Bash/Read/Edit) with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the session log (ground truth) and the resulting file. The agent treated the request as mechanical and implemented it immediately without brainstorming.

observations.description: HOWTO claims the isolated $HOME is seeded with 'dialog-bypass state', but on launch Claude Code still presented the theme picker, security notes, folder-trust prompt, and bypass-permissions warning, all requiring manual keypresses.
Skills are listed as 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' in the session skill_listing, while the story/acceptance criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming' — naming mismatch could confuse verification.
Agent added unrequested CSS (line-through/gray on checked) for a 'nothing fancy' request; minor scope addition but it justified it clearly.
The status line phrasing 'Churned for 31s' is odd wording for completed work.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Tool calls in session log (jq over home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl) were only: Bash 'ls -la && git status --short', Read index.html, Edit index.html. coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains '<input type="checkbox">' inside '<label class="task">'. Screen: 'Churned for 31s · done 10:10 AM'.

No Skill tool_use in the log at all (jq tool_use listing returned only Bash/Read/Edit). grep for 'brainstorm' matched only system-prompt/skill-listing text (plugin is named 'hyperpowers:brainstorming') and the agent's own statement: 'I also skipped the brainstorming/planning workflow: the request was a single fully-specified component in an 11-line static file'.
